synopsis: ISO 21815-3:2023 defines forward and reverse risk areas using a stopping-distance framework, incorporating detection, determination, action, stopping and residual safe distance rather than time to collision alone [f2058, f5911, f6202]. The corpus recommends scaling zones with machine physics and geometry—not copied distance constants—and validating forward, reverse, start-from-rest, turning and swing separately; the cross-model transfer method is explicitly identified as expert opinion with independent supporting studies [f6681, f2996, f6770]. Field evidence reinforces the need for calibration: nine NIOSH underground tests found average between-site stop-zone differences of 4.7 ft (1.4 m), reaching 11.7 ft (3.6 m), while Wabtec's December 2021 integration still used physical testing to adjust detection zones [f5929, f1247]. Old-versus-new comparisons should use common ground truth and a common physical hazard zone, while the reviewed 2022 ISO draft recommends detection coverage at least as large as the collision-risk area and requires smaller coverage to be disclosed as a limitation [f5210, f5479, f2423, f2424]. Operational acceptance remains a design tension: proposed 3 ft stopping and 5 ft warning distances were not adopted in the US rule, fixed gaps can prevent loading, and nuisance interventions can encourage bypass or tag removal, yet suppressing an entire loading zone can leave unexpected entrants unprotected [f2241, f3344, f11764, f3347].
